nodes.description: The medial habenula projects almost exclusively to the interpeduncular nucleus, and alpha-5-containing receptors on that projection carry an inhibitory motivational signal that the higher nicotine doses recruit. Removing or knocking down the alpha-5 subunit, or inactivating the interpeduncular nucleus, raises nicotine intake without altering how rewarding low doses are, so the circuit is a brake on consumption rather than a contributor to reward. Reduced signalling here is the mechanism through which the CHRNA5 risk allele is thought to act in smokers; that step is inferred from the direction of the human association rather than measured in people, which is why the node is provisional.

nodes.description: The cues that accompany smoking acquire motivational value through pavlovian learning, and control over seeking migrates from goal-directed to habitual as it moves from ventral to more dorsal striatum. In smoking this learning is unusually heavily rehearsed: a pack-a-day smoker repeats the drug-cue pairing on the order of two hundred times a day, which is an order of magnitude more trials than most other drugs of abuse deliver.

nodes.description: CYP2A6 performs most of the conversion of nicotine to cotinine, so its activity sets how fast brain nicotine falls between cigarettes. The ratio of 3'-hydroxycotinine to cotinine in a single sample reads that activity out, which makes the rate measurable in a clinic. Faster clearance means a shorter interval before the receptor population is unoccupied again, and in a randomised trial it changes which pharmacotherapy works: it is the one node in this entry with an established treatment-selection consequence.
nodes.id: Nicotine Clearance Rate Set by CYP2A6 Activity

The DSM-IV set, which the DSM-5 criteria retain, is depressed mood, insomnia, irritability, anxiety, difficulty concentrating, restlessness, decreased heart rate and increased appetite, with craving alongside. More dependent smokers do not simply report more symptoms: they report a syndromal pattern, where smokers with comorbid anxiety, depression or disordered eating report the symptoms their own disorder resembles.

nodes.description: A route that delivers nicotine without combustion, used for cessation in many countries. In the Cochrane component network meta-analysis it was among the three most effective interventions, alongside varenicline and cytisine, on high-certainty evidence. It is also the clearest case of why this entry is bound to nicotine dependence rather than to tobacco use disorder: a patient who switches completely remains dependent on nicotine while no longer being a tobacco user, and that is a case the binding, and so this entry, covers. Its regulatory status varies by country and is not recorded here.

nodes.description: Inhaled nicotine reaches the brain within seconds of a puff and acts as an agonist at neuronal nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, which are ligand-gated cation channels assembled from five subunits. The subtypes that carry the addictive effects are the high-affinity heteromers containing alpha-4 and beta-2; the beta-2 subunit is required for nicotine to reach the dopamine system at all, and selective activation of alpha-4-containing receptors is on its own enough to produce reinforcement, tolerance and sensitisation.

nodes.description: Chronic nicotine increases the number of high-affinity beta-2-containing receptors while a large fraction of them sit desensitised at the concentrations smoking sustains. In smokers the excess binding is measurable in vivo and does not return to never-smoker levels for weeks after the last cigarette, which is the molecular state the early abstinent patient is in. The upregulation is nicotine-specific rather than part of the shared addiction cycle, so it stays on this entry.

nodes.description: A high-affinity partial agonist occupies the alpha-4-beta-2 receptor, desensitising it and activating it weakly. The dual action is the point: the weak activation substitutes for some of the withdrawal relief nicotine would give, and the occupancy blunts the reinforcement a cigarette smoked on top of it would produce. This node exists as the target the two partial-agonist treatments below point at.
nodes.id: Partial Agonist Occupancy of Alpha4Beta2 Nicotinic Receptors

nodes.description: Common and low-frequency variation at the CHRNA5-CHRNA3-CHRNB4 cluster on chromosome 15q25 shifts liability to dependence and to heavy smoking. It is the strongest and most replicated signal in the trait, and its lead allele reduces the function of the alpha-5 subunit rather than increasing it, which is why the downstream edge runs to a loss of the aversion brake rather than to a gain in reward. The molecular function bound here is that of the receptor these three subunits assemble into, marked DECREASED for the lead allele's direction of effect. Liability carried by CYP2A6 is a separate, pharmacokinetic route and is curated on the clearance node.

nodes.description: Abstinence from nicotine lowers the function of the dopamine component of the reward system and recruits the extended-amygdala stress neurotransmitters, so that smoking comes to relieve a negative state rather than to produce a positive one. This is the opponent-process adaptation the addiction cycle module names as its key conformance target, and it is the stage at which nicotine dependence becomes self-sustaining: the patient now has a reason to smoke that does not depend on nicotine being pleasant.

nodes.description: The dependence maintains a daily inhaled exposure to tobacco combustion products. The node is kept so the pathograph does not stop at the psychiatric syndrome and leave the burden unexplained.

evidence.snippet: The study did not show a significant increase in neuropsychiatric adverse events attributable to varenicline or bupropion relative to nicotine patch or placebo.

nodes.description: Nicotinic agonism on ventral tegmental dopaminergic neurons raises their firing rate and, more specifically, the number and length of phasic bursts. Because the nucleus accumbens shell and the dorsolateral striatum have different frequency dependences for dopamine release, the shift towards bursting raises dopamine preferentially in the shell. This is the step nicotine shares with every other drug of abuse, and the step the addiction cycle module anchors.
nodes.id: Ventral Tegmental Dopamine Neuron Activation and Mesolimbic Dopamine Release

evidence.reference_title: Drugs abused by humans preferentially increase synaptic dopamine concentrations in the mesolimbic system of freely moving rats.
evidence.snippet: Drugs abused by humans (e.g., opiates, ethanol, nicotine, amphetamine, and cocaine) increased extracellular dopamine concentrations in both areas, but especially in the accumbens, and elicited hypermotility at low doses.

evidence.reference_title: Dopamine signaling differences in the nucleus accumbens and dorsal striatum exploited by nicotine.
evidence.snippet: Nicotine administration increased the firing frequency of dopamine neurons and specifically increased the number and the length of phasic burst firing.

evidence.reference_title: Dopamine signaling differences in the nucleus accumbens and dorsal striatum exploited by nicotine.
evidence.snippet: By favoring release from bursts while depressing release from tonic signals, nicotine spreads the range of dopamine signaling and effectively increases the signal-to-noise relationship along dopamine afferents.

nodes.description: A common nonsynonymous coding variant, D398N, in the alpha-5 subunit. Associated with nicotine dependence, heaviness of smoking, cessation, and with smoking-related lung cancer and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Functionally it reduces alpha-5 subunit function.
